summary: Registering a GitHub OAuth app is self-serve, with no GitHub review or payment, so users can connect as soon as the app is registered. The main thing that can hold up launch is that organizations with OAuth app access restrictions block members from authorizing your app.

gates.title: Any GitHub account can register an OAuth app
No test or development mode with limits
No GitHub review before users can connect
Organizations with access restrictions block your app
gates.what: When an organization has OAuth app access restrictions on, its members cannot authorize your app for organization resources. New organizations have restrictions enabled by default.
gates.where: Organization Settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy. The organization owner acts here, not you.
gates.todo: Tell users in restricted organizations to request approval for your app from their organization owner.

gates.title: No paid plan needed for production use

requirements.text: A GitHub account, or admin access to an organization that will own the app
A homepage URL for the app
A redirect URI for your app (up to 10 allowed)

steps.text: Open Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps and click New OAuth App.
steps.detail: To own the app under an organization, start from that organization's settings instead of your personal ones.

steps.text: Fill in Application name, Homepage URL and Application description.
steps.why: Users see these when they authorize your app. Name and homepage are required; the description is optional.

steps.text: Under Redirect URIs, enter the URL GitHub should send users back to after they authorize.
steps.why: The redirect_uri your app sends must match one of these, or authorization fails.
steps.detail: Up to 10, via Add redirect URI. Leave Allow wildcard matching off unless you control every subdomain and path. GitHub's docs still call this field "Authorization callback URL".

steps.text: Leave Enable Device Flow unchecked unless your app has no browser (a CLI, IoT device or headless tool).
steps.why: Off by default. It skips redirect URIs, so it can be abused to impersonate your app in phishing attacks.

steps.text: Keep Expire user access tokens checked.
steps.why: On by default so a leaked token dies within 8 hours; your app renews tokens with a refresh token. Turn it off only if your app can't handle refresh yet.

steps.text: Click Register application, then copy the client ID and generate a client secret.
steps.detail: Keep the client secret out of client-side code.

blockers.problem: Users in an organization cannot grant your app access to its resources.
blockers.fix: The organization has OAuth app access restrictions on. The user requests approval, and an organization owner approves it under OAuth app policy.

blockers.problem: Authorization fails with a redirect_uri error.
blockers.fix: Send a redirect_uri that matches a registered callback URL, or omit the parameter to use the default.
GitHub revokes an OAuth token unused for a year. Send the user through authorization again.

claims.statement: An OAuth app can be registered under a personal account or any organization the developer administers.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.

claims.statement: No test or development mode with limits is mentioned on the OAuth app creation page.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs

claims.statement: No provider review or verification step is mentioned on the OAuth app creation page.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs

claims.statement: Organizations with OAuth app access restrictions block members from authorizing OAuth app access to organization resources.
claims.sourceTitle: About OAuth app access restrictions - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access to organization resources.

claims.statement: New organizations have restrictions enabled by default.
claims.sourceTitle: About OAuth app access restrictions - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default.

claims.statement: Organization owners can approve or deny a member's request for OAuth app access.
claims.sourceTitle: Approving OAuth apps for your organization - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: When an organization member or outside collaborator requests OAuth app access to organization resources, organization owners can approve or deny the request.

claims.statement: An OAuth app's requests count toward the user's personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
claims.sourceTitle: Rate limits for the REST API - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

claims.statement: No recurring re-verification or audit is mentioned in the token expiration page.
claims.sourceTitle: Token expiration and revocation - GitHub Docs

claims.statement: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

claims.statement: If your redirect_uri doesn't match what you registered, GitHub redirects to your registered callback URL with an error.
claims.sourceTitle: Troubleshooting authorization request errors - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: If you provide a redirect_uri that doesn't match what you've registered with your application, GitHub will redirect to the registered callback URL with the following parameters summarizing the error:

claims.statement: Device flow must be enabled in the app settings before use.
claims.sourceTitle: Authorizing OAuth apps - GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs
claims.quote: Before you can use the device flow to authorize and identify users, you must first enable it in your app's settings.

claims.statement: Expiring tokens last eight hours, with refresh tokens expiring after six months without use.
claims.sourceTitle: Authorizing OAuth apps - GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs
claims.quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.

claims.statement: The client secret must stay out of client-side code.
claims.sourceTitle: Rate limits for the REST API - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: Never include your app's client secret in client-side code or in code that runs on a user device.

claims.statement: OAuth tokens unused for a year are revoked.
claims.sourceTitle: Token expiration and revocation - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: GitHub will automatically revoke an OAuth token or personal access token when the token hasn't been used in one year.

claims.statement: Expire user access tokens is enabled by default.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: Expire user access tokens is enabled by default.

claims.statement: Device flow lets users sign in to apps without a browser, such as CLI tools.
claims.sourceTitle: Authorizing OAuth apps - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: The device flow allows you to authorize users for a headless application, such as a CLI tool or the Git Credential Manager

claims.statement: Device flow doesn't use redirect URIs, so an attacker can use it to impersonate your app in a phishing attack.
claims.sourceTitle: Best practices for creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: The device flow does not require redirect URIs at all, which means that an attacker can use the device flow to remotely impersonate your app as part of a phishing attack.

claims.statement: Expiring tokens enforce regular token rotation and reduce the impact of a compromised token.
claims.sourceTitle: Authorizing OAuth apps - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: To enforce regular token rotation and reduce the impact of a compromised token, you can configure your OAuth app to get access tokens that expire.

claims.statement: On the live registration form, the callback field is a "Redirect URIs" section: up to 10 URIs, added with "Add redirect URI", each with an "Allow wildcard matching" checkbox. GitHub's docs still call it "Authorization callback URL".
claims.sourceTitle: GitHub: Register a new OAuth app (live form)
claims.quote: You may add up to 10 redirect URIs.
claims.note: Observed by a person on the live form on 2026-10-28 (screenshot).

claims.statement: Wildcard matching sends tokens to every subdomain and path of the redirect URI; GitHub advises enabling it only if you control all of them.
claims.sourceTitle: GitHub: Register a new OAuth app (live form)
claims.quote: Only enable this if you are sure you have control over all possible matches.
claims.note: Text on the live form, observed 2026-10-28.

claims.statement: On the live form, Enable Device Flow is unchecked and Expire user access tokens is checked by default.
claims.sourceTitle: GitHub: Register a new OAuth app (live form)
claims.note: Observed by a person on the live form on 2026-10-28 (screenshot). Matches the docs.

claims.statement: The registration form asks for the full URL of your app's website as the Homepage URL.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: In "Homepage URL", type the full URL to your app's website.

claims.statement: GitHub advises enabling device flow only for CLIs, IoT devices or headless systems.
claims.sourceTitle: Best practices for creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: For this reason, do not enable the device flow for your application unless you are using the app in a constrained environment (CLIs, IoT devices, or headless systems).

claims.statement: No paid plan is mentioned as a requirement on GitHub's OAuth app creation page.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.note: Absence claim: the page that would state a paid requirement doesn't mention one.

reviewNote: Reviewed by a person on 2026-10-28: every step checked against the live registration form (steps 1–5) or GitHub's docs (step 6). Corrections: device flow and token expiry explained from GitHub's docs, false 'docs conflict' note removed, non-setup step removed, callback field renamed to Redirect URIs to match the live form. On 2026-10-29 the new support check flagged claims that combined two facts under one quote; each was split or re-quoted so every claim states exactly what its quote says.
